questions.q: What does the GRAB model stand for?
a: Goal, results, audience, budget, brand
Growth, reach, ads, budget, branding
Goal, reach, analysis, bids, buyers
Group, results, audience, bids, brand
questions.why: Lesson 1 walks through goal, results, audience, budget and brand.

questions.q: Why does Mars insist on a specific goal before anything else?
a: Without a finish line you cannot tell if it worked
Facebook only allows one goal per account
A goal automatically sets your budget
Specific goals lower the price of ads
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares it to running a marathon without a finish line.

questions.q: How does the 20/30/50 rule split a campaign budget?
a: Twenty on all ads, thirty on the best, fifty on the best plus refined targeting
Fifty on all ads, thirty on the best, twenty on targeting
Twenty on targeting, thirty on creative, fifty on placement
Equal thirds across testing, scaling and retargeting
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes testing broadly, then narrowing as data arrives.

questions.q: Why keep the target audience under 300,000 people?
a: A smaller sample makes it easier to see what works
Facebook charges more for large audiences
Large audiences cannot be saved
Small audiences always convert at a fixed rate
questions.why: Lesson 3 ties a narrow audience to measurable results.

questions.q: What is the difference between efficient and effective ad spending?
a: Efficient spends correctly; effective spends on the right things
Efficient spends more; effective spends less
Efficient targets everyone; effective targets no one
Efficient is short-term; effective is long-term
questions.why: Lesson 2 says effectiveness means picking the right things first.
